The scooter gleamed in the parking area of Eshaan's building. Jomon walked around it twice. "Looks almost new. Eighteen thousand, you said?"
Eshaan had rehearsed the good parts: new tyres, full service record, one owner. On the way down, though, he had asked himself a plain question: if I were buying this, what would I want to know? He didn't bother with the scuffed mirror or the old sticker; those wouldn't change anyone's mind.
"Before you decide," he said, "it stood in water during last year's floods. The mechanic fixed the wiring, but on very wet mornings it sometimes takes a few tries to start."
Jomon's eyebrows went up. "That changes the price."
"I know."
They settled on fifteen. Jomon shook his hand. "You could have kept quiet, you know."
"Then you'd find out in July," Eshaan said.

qa.q: What happened to the scooter during last year's floods?
qa.a: It stood in water, and the mechanic fixed the wiring.

qa.q: What does Eshaan's question to himself on the way down show about his thinking?
qa.a: It shows he wanted to think from Jomon's side and share what a buyer would really need to know, even if it cost him.

qa.q: Why was the flood worth mentioning when the scuffed mirror was not?
qa.a: The flood could change Jomon's decision and the price, while the scuffed mirror would not change anyone's mind.

qa.q: How does Jomon see Eshaan after hearing about the flood?
qa.a: Jomon is surprised but seems to respect him, saying Eshaan could have kept quiet and shaking his hand on the deal.

grounding: An adult selling a scooter asks what the buyer would want to know and plainly shares the flood damage, even though it lowers the price.

"So," Vandana said, stirring her coffee, "our families have already said everything nice about us."
Dhruv laughed. "They have. Can I tell you one thing they probably left out?"
"Please."
"My father had a stroke last year. I've decided to stay in my hometown and look after him. I won't be moving to a big city, even for a better job."
Vandana put her spoon down. "Why tell me at the first meeting?"
"Because if I were you, it would change what I'm deciding. I'd rather you know now than feel tricked later."
"Most people would wait."
"I know. It might cost me this."
She looked at him for a long moment. "It hasn't cost you anything with me yet. Tell me about your father."

qa.q: What has Dhruv decided to do about his father?
qa.a: Dhruv has decided to stay in his hometown and look after him.

qa.q: How did Dhruv feel about sharing this at the first meeting, and why do it anyway?
qa.a: Dhruv felt nervous that it might cost him the match, but he would rather Vandana know now than feel tricked later.

qa.q: What makes Dhruv's disclosure wise rather than oversharing?
qa.a: He chose the one fact that affects her decision, where they would live, and said it plainly without listing every private detail.

qa.q: How might Vandana's view of Dhruv change after he speaks up?
qa.a: She may trust him more because he risked the match to be honest, which is why she asks to hear about his father.

grounding: At a first marriage meeting a young man volunteers the fact that would change the other person's choice, even though it may cost him.

passage:
I'm Charu, and last month I sold my old scooter to Rekha, a new colleague who had just moved to the city.
She loved it at first sight. Bright red, new seat cover, starts in one kick. She was already reaching for her phone to pay.
Then I thought: what would I want to know if I were her? Not every scratch. But the rear brake had been soft for weeks, and my mechanic had said it needed proper work.
"Before you decide," I said, "the rear brake is weak. It's safe to ride slowly, but it needs repair soon. I should have fixed it."
Her face fell a little. She asked a few questions, then offered less, and I agreed.
I lost some money. But on Monday she brought me a box of sweets from her hometown, and she's the first person I trust at work now.

qa.q: What was wrong with the scooter?
qa.a: The rear brake had been soft for weeks and needed proper work.

qa.q: How did Rekha feel when Charu mentioned the brake?
qa.a: Rekha felt a little disappointed at first, but later grateful, since she brought Charu sweets and became a trusted colleague.

qa.q: Which question helped Charu decide what to say?
qa.a: Charu asked what Charu would want to know in Rekha's place, which pointed to the brake, not every scratch.

qa.q: How might things have gone if Charu had stayed silent about the brake?
qa.a: Rekha might have found out while riding, felt deceived, and never trusted Charu at work.

grounding: It shows an adult asking what the buyer would want to know and plainly stating the brake problem, even though it cost the narrator.

passage:
Team lead's note, handover week, Thursday.
Today Pankaj handed the client dashboard project to Gopika before his transfer to the Hyderabad office. I sat in on the handover.
He could have given a clean picture: the design is done, the client likes the colours, the code is mostly finished. All true. Instead, before Gopika opened her laptop, he said, "Three things you need to know first. The client has complained twice about delays. The login page breaks on older phones. And I promised a demo on the 12th that we can't really make."
I could see it cost him. His voice was tight, and he knew I was listening. Gopika wrote everything down and asked, "Anything else that would change what I do in week one?" He thought and said, "No, that's the list."
After he left, I told Gopika we'd move the demo together. I also told Pankaj his handover was the most useful one I've seen this year.

qa.q: What date was the demo Pankaj promised?
qa.a: He promised a demo on the 12th.

qa.q: What does Pankaj's tight voice suggest about his feelings?
qa.a: It suggests he felt nervous and embarrassed, since admitting the delays and broken login made him look bad in front of the team lead.

qa.q: What would you advise someone handing over a project, based on this note?
qa.a: Share first the few problems that would change the next person's choices, as Pankaj did, rather than only the finished parts.

qa.q: How does Gopika experience the handover?
qa.a: Gopika is able to start with the real problems in view, which lets her plan week one and move the demo instead of being surprised.

grounding: A team lead records an adult plainly volunteering the problems that would change a colleague's decisions, even at a cost to himself.

passage:
Sunday night.
Met Samir and his family today at the café near the lake. Third meeting. His mother was already talking about dates in winter.
I had rehearsed saying it in the auto: I've been offered two more years on the research project in Germany, and I want to take it. I kept waiting for a better moment. There was no better moment.
So when Samir and I walked to the water, I just said it. "Before anyone plans anything, you should know I'm going to Germany in August for two years. I'd understand if that changes things."
He was quiet for a long time. Then he said, "Thank you for telling me now and not after."
I don't know what he'll decide. My stomach is still in knots. But I'm Yamini, and I don't want a marriage that starts with me hiding the biggest thing in my life. Whatever he chooses, he'll be choosing me as I am.

qa.q: Where did Yamini meet Samir and his family?
qa.a: At the café near the lake.

qa.q: How is Yamini feeling as she writes the diary entry?
qa.a: Yamini feels anxious, with her stomach still in knots, but also steady because she said the important thing before any plans were made.

qa.q: What did Yamini do that fits a wise way of handling this choice?
qa.a: Yamini told Samir plainly about the two years in Germany before anyone planned dates, because that fact would change his decision.

qa.q: How does Samir see Yamini's honesty?
qa.a: Samir seems grateful, thanking Yamini for telling him now and not after, even though he needs time to think.

grounding: It shows an adult volunteering the one fact that would change a marriage decision, even though it may cost the match.
